title: Last Remaining Integer After Alternating Deletion Operations
summary: Given an integer n, write the integers from 1 to n in sequence.
statement: Given an integer n, write the integers from 1 to n in sequence. Alternately apply two operations: Operation 1 deletes every second number from the left, and Operation 2 deletes every second number from the right. Continue until one integer remains, which is the output.
constraints: Starting from [1..n], alternately delete every second item counted from the left and then from the right.
The first item counted from either side is kept; return the sole survivor.
hints: The remaining sequence is always an arithmetic progression described by first, step, and length.
A left round keeps positions 0,2,…; a right round starts at position one only when the current length is even.
Update the first value for that even right round, double the step, and replace length by ceil(length/2).
These state updates exactly describe the retained indices, and logarithmically many rounds reduce the length to one.
editorial: These state updates exactly describe the retained indices, and logarithmically many rounds reduce the length to one.

tests.explanation: Keeping alternating positions from the left, right, then left yields [1,3,5,7], [3,7], and finally 3.
